decision.detail: I push back from the coffee table. The mug is still warm; I leave it. I pull the small Sony recorder and one lavalier mic out of my satchel, clip the mic to my jacket so it doesn't rattle, set the recorder in my breast pocket. I stand. I turn to the four of them. I say two sentences. I walk to the door. I push it open. February air hits my throat. I start walking south toward the Rialto. Two blocks. The diesel smell is still there from the van. My hands are in my pockets. I'm not looking at my phone. I'm counting the crosswalks.
decision.intention: Be in the Rialto booth before the last reel loads onto the regional line. Sit beside Alma, not across. Let her talk. Record it. Send the file to Pittsburgh tonight with no title, no slug, no broadcast package. One voice, one daughter, one machine about to stop.
decision.words: Ballroom's yours. I'm on the Rialto. One mic, one cable, a chair if her back's bad. I'll handle the rest.
